   216→
   217→- **Creating alerts in Grafana UI without version control:** Always define as JSON in repo, deploy via API script

   220→- **Reducing timeouts without checking retry behavior:** Some operations retry on timeout; reducing timeout without adjusting retry config can cause cascading failures

   233→## Common Pitfalls
   234→
   235→### Pitfall 1: Grafana Cloud datasource UID mismatch
   236→
   237→**What goes wrong:** Alert rules reference a datasource UID that doesn't match the Grafana Cloud Mimir instance
   238→**Why it happens:** Dashboard JSON uses template variable `${DS_GRAFANA_CLOUD_METRICS}` but alert rules need the actual resolved UID
   239→**How to avoid:** Query the Grafana Cloud API for the actual Mimir datasource UID before provisioning, or use the Grafana UI to find it: Settings > Data Sources > Prometheus/Mimir > copy UID from the URL
   240→**Warning signs:** Alert rules show "No data" even though dashboard panels work
   241→
   242→### Pitfall 2: histogram_quantile returns NaN when no data
   243→
   244→**What goes wrong:** Alert fires on "no data" state because `histogram_quantile()` returns NaN when there are no observations in the window
   245→**Why it happens:** Low-traffic operations may have no samples in a 5m window
   246→**How to avoid:** Set `noDataState: "OK"` in alert rule definition. Only alert when the quantile exceeds a threshold AND data exists
   247→**Warning signs:** Constant alert notifications during low-traffic periods
   248→
   249→### Pitfall 3: Rate window too short for scrape interval
   250→
   251→**What goes wrong:** `rate()` over 1m with 30s scrape interval produces unreliable results
   252→**Why it happens:** Prometheus needs at least 2 data points in a range to calculate rate; with 30s scrape, a 1m window only guarantees 2-3 points
   253→**How to avoid:** Use `rate(...[5m])` minimum for a 30s scrape interval (gives ~10 data points per window)
   254→**Warning signs:** Noisy/spiky alert evaluations
   255→
   256→### Pitfall 4: Timeout reduction causes cascade failures
   257→
   258→**What goes wrong:** Reducing a timeout (e.g., Kubo 30s -> 10s) causes operations to fail that would have succeeded with the longer timeout, triggering retries that compound the problem
   259→**Why it happens:** The 2-3x p99 formula works for typical load, but under high concurrency (50+ clients), p99 is much higher than under normal load
   260→**How to avoid:** Use the single-client or low-concurrency (5 client) p99 baselines for timeout derivation, NOT the 50-client stress test values. Validate with the load test harness at representative concurrency (5-10 clients)
   261→**Warning signs:** Load test threshold violations after timeout changes
   262→
   263→### Pitfall 5: Alerting on the wrong histogram
   264→
   265→**What goes wrong:** Alerts fire on `cipherbox_ipfs_ipns_duration_seconds` when they should fire on `cipherbox_ipns_resolve_duration_seconds`
   266→**Why it happens:** The project has TWO resolve histograms: the general IPFS/IPNS one (Phase 18) and the dedicated IPNS resolve one (Phase 19). They have different labels.
   267→**How to avoid:** Use the Phase 19 histograms for IPNS-specific alerts: `cipherbox_ipns_resolve_duration_seconds` (source/outcome labels) and `cipherbox_ipns_publish_duration_seconds` (outcome label). Use the general `cipherbox_ipfs_ipns_duration_seconds` for IPFS pin/cat alerts.
   268→**Warning signs:** Alert expressions don't match any time series
